Document: # Breathing and oxygen deprivation Insufficient breathing causes suffocation damage after the body's initial reserve runs out. Breathing, masks and gas exchange otherwise work as before. - Outside critical condition, sustained suffocation adds 1.5 damage per second. Adequate breathing removes 0.625 per second. - In either critical condition, sustained suffocation adds 0.33 damage per second. Natural breathing alone no longer removes this damage: use oxygen medicine or full CPR. - Suffocation causes unconsciousness at half the body's soft critical damage threshold: normally 50 for a human. Bodies without a separate soft critical threshold use half their first critical threshold. - This early unconsciousness does not prevent natural breathing. Restoring suitable air prevents further suffocation; treatment below the threshold removes the oxygen-related unconsciousness. Other causes of unconsciousness, including revival recovery and sedation, can keep a patient unconscious after their oxygen damage improves.
